newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Euro Disney loss widens, charges rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro Disney loss widens, charges rise.

text.p: Euro Disney said on Tuesday its losses widened in the first half of 1996/97 as rising debt expenses swallowed up income generated by the Disneyland Paris theme park.
Euro Disney reported a net loss of 210 million francs ($36 million) for the six months to March 31, its winter season, compared with a loss of 169 million for the first half of 1995/96.
The deterioration in its results, the first year-on-year downturn after more than two years of improvement, was due to a 68 million franc jump in charges to 356 million francs.

The surge in lease and financial expenses had been expected as Euro Disney took on payments that had been temporarily waived by a 1994 debt restructuring accord to keep the fledgling company from collapsing under a huge debt burden.

First-half income before charges more than doubled to 120 million francs from 58 million on sales of 2.17 billion francs, helped by a 12.5 percent rise in attendance, higher hotel occupancy rates and increased spending per visitor.
The commercial appeal of Euro Disney, 39 percent owned by The Walt Disney Co., is no longer in doubt. It celebrated its fifth anniversary last month as Europe's top tourist attraction.

"The success of Disneyland Paris is growing, as is our ability to manage the seasonal fluctuations in the business. However, growth in the high season remains vital to counter the sharp increases in financial charges," chairman Gilles Pelisson said in the earnings statement.
The company traditionally loses money in the winter season but more than compensates during the April-September high season and has reported full-year profits for the past two years.

The first-half results were in line with stock market expectations. But the share price was down one percent at 9.80 francs as the results reminded investors that any gains in operating profit will go to pay back the banks and Disney.

As part of the repayment schedule set out in the 1994 debt agreement, Euro Disney's debt expenses began climbing last year. The biggest increase was pencilled in for the 1996/97 fiscal year and is estimated by the company at 200 million francs.
Debt charges will rise by a further 120 million francs in 1997/98 and by 100 million in 1998/99.
In addition, royalty and management fees to Disney -- which had also been waived -- kick in after 1998.

"Together, royalty and fee payments will further pressure pretax earnings by approximately 205 million francs in 1999 and 215 million francs in 2000," U.S. broker Goldman Sachs said in a report. It sees no earnings per share growth before 2002.
Euro Disney's debt stood at 15.1 billion francs in the year to September 30.
"For a long time to come, revenues will be absorbed by the financial charges," said share analyst Antoine Nodet at Paris brokerage Dupont Denant.

"In addition, the economic climate isn't favourable. They can't raise prices. They can count only on volumes," he said. He is forecasting a drop in 1996/97 full-year pre-exceptional profit to 110 million francs from 156 million.
A spokesman for Euro Disney said the company was pleased with the first-half results, given the weak economy and rise in expenses. "Offsetting this big increase wasn't easy," he said.

Euro Disney said the decision to hold prices this year at 1996 levels was helping visitor attendance and hotel occupancy but "limiting the company's potential to improve its margins". ($ = 5.832 French Francs)
